title: FactoryOutcome
description: A Factory delivery-workflow record: one requested outcome (bug fix, feature, or new app) with its bounded plan and acceptance criteria, plus the workflow's own lifecycle state (spec-factory.md §2/§9). Fulfils demand `factory-20260911-interface-extraction` criterion 1. This is Factory's OWN new workflow ID, never an edit of an existing `app.mission` (app-studio) record — `source` (see `$defs/continuationSource`) is the only link back to legacy history, and it is additive: publishing this schema changes nothing about `app.mission`'s own shape or lifecycle. Modeled from the repo's own proven `factory.domain` module (`Intake`, `new_mission`), not invented ahead of what actually ships.

id.description: Factory's own workflow record identifier — a new id minted at intake, never an app-studio mission id.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency counter for this record; incremented on every accepted mutation.

app.description: Functional name (D002) of the target app repo this outcome is delivered into.

kind.description: Which of the three proportional workflow shapes this outcome runs (spec-factory.md §2) — each has its own ordered phase sequence.

risk.description: Low-risk plans may auto-release on a passing plan approval; high-risk work always needs a separate release decision at the candidate revision. Escalated to `high` automatically when the requested outcome text matches a sensitive-work pattern (auth/session/password/security/payment/delete/migration), even if intake left it at `low`.

title.description: Short human title for the requested outcome.

plan.description: The bounded implementation plan an owner approved (or will approve) at this outcome's `planHash`.

criteria.description: Requested outcomes with their acceptance test, one entry per criterion id. IDs are unique within one record.

phase.description: Current step in this outcome's `kind`-specific workflow sequence (e.g. `implement`, `test`, `deploy`, `verify`, or `complete`). The full ordered sequence is workflow-shape-specific and lives in Factory's own code, not duplicated here — this field is free text over that private enum so a new phase name never becomes a breaking schema change.

status.description: Record-level lifecycle. Only `active` records accept new evidence or decisions (spec-factory.md §3 — archived/partial/complete records are read-only).

candidate.description: The revision (commit SHA or equivalent) currently under implementation/test/release for this outcome. Empty string before a candidate exists.

paused.description: True while future dispatch is paused; an already-active run may still be in flight (spec-factory.md's recovery posture — pausing never claims to have stopped a live run).

source.description: Present only when this outcome is a continuation of a terminal legacy app-studio mission. Absent for outcomes requested directly against an app with no such lineage.

parent.description: This outcome's own `id` if it superseded an earlier Factory outcome (e.g. a new-app continuation carrying forward an unfinished checkpoint), else `null`.

followup.description: The `id` of a later Factory outcome that superseded this one, else `null`. Inverse of `parent`.

approvals.description: Owner decisions recorded against this outcome's plan/release checksums (spec-factory.md's separate-facts rule — a plan approval and a release approval are always distinct entries).

checkpoint.description: This outcome's current recovery checkpoint. Present (possibly empty) from creation onward.

id.description: Unique (within the outcome) identifier this criterion is referenced by from evidence and completion checks.

outcome.description: What must be true when this criterion is met.

acceptance.description: How the criterion will be verified.

kind.description: A plan approval authorizes implementation at the current `planHash`; a release approval authorizes deploying `revision` — always a separate, explicit decision (spec-factory.md §3: 'never approve its own work').

planHash.description: SHA-256 over the outcome's `app`/`kind`/`risk`/`plan`/`criteria` at approval time — binds this decision to one exact scope.

revision.description: The candidate revision this approval concerns; empty string for a plan approval made before a candidate exists.

autoRelease.description: True when a plan approval also pre-authorized low-risk auto-release; always `false` for a `release`-kind approval and never usable for `risk: high` work.

note.description: The concrete reason recorded with this decision — never a bare approve/reject flag.
